alternatives.argument: The algorithm item fully defines the finite oracle, projection update, early failure record, full-run average, tie rule, and budget status; projection existence is supplied by the nearest-point theorem. No convergence fact is delegated to Shor.
The local proof applies the projection variational inequality, expands squared distances, and substitutes the exact convex subgradient inequality.

The local proof sums the one-step inequalities, telescopes the distance, bounds each subgradient norm and initial distance, then applies finite Jensen and the minimum-versus-weighted-average inequality.
The corollary substitutes alpha=R/(G sqrt(N)) into the proved bound; the R=0 and G=0 boundaries are handled separately without using a zero stepsize.

The local proof shows the loop makes at most N oracle requests, preserves feasibility by unique projection, returns immediately on failure, and forms the average and least-index best only after all calls succeed.

alternatives.argument: The algorithm explicitly defines the full-memory finite maximum of supporting affine cuts, unique quadratic model candidate, predicted decrease, serious/null acceptance, append rule, oracle failure, and finite statuses. It makes no convergence assertion.

The local proof bounds the model below by one affine cut, completes the square to obtain bounded sublevels, proves continuity of the finite maximum plus quadratic, applies Heine–Borel and the extreme-value theorem, and uses the strict midpoint identity for uniqueness.

The proof compares the model objective at its minimizer z and the exact proximal point p, uses M≤F to obtain Q_F(z)≤Q_F(p)+e, then applies the locally proved quadratic-growth inequality to obtain ||z-p||²≤4te.

The complete local proof adds compact initial sublevel, continuity, positive predicted decreases, exact serious acceptance, and e_k→0; proximal nonexpansiveness identifies candidate limits, and a contradiction with summable center decreases proves every accumulation point globally minimizes F. It does not infer e_k→0 from full memory.
The example computes both exact quadratic model minimizers and verifies the subgradient cuts, null-step test, and serious-step test by direct arithmetic.
The local proof uses the unique model minimizer, the explicit oracle/P<=0 statuses, and a counter increment on every completed serious/null trial to prove return within N trials.
